profile.headline: Principal Software Engineer, Desktop at Blurb
profile.summary:
• 10 years experience developing cross-platform GUI software in C++ with Qt.
• Architected, built, and maintained Blurb's flagship desktop book-making tool.
• Effectively used various design patterns to manage complex product requirements and technical challenges.
• I learn fast and that makes me versatile. I can jump into existing code bases and learn new programming languages and design patterns with ease.

positions.title: Principal Software Engineer, Desktop
positions.description:
• Continue development of BookWright - Blurb's flagship desktop tool written in C++ and Qt.
• Responsible for all code architecture planning and decisions with respect to feature implementation and code redesigns in BookWright.
• Collaborate with the product, marketing, and customer support teams to determine what features we can successfully implement and ship.
• Facilitate weekly engineering meetings and curate presentations for Blurb's developers to share knowledge of our systems.
• Serve on the tech leads team to discuss and resolve issues facing engineering as a whole.
• Run postgres queries in our analytics database to analyze BookWright feature usage.
• Contributed to updating our build and deploy systems for a data center move.
• Designed and implemented changes to the auto-updater system so we can quickly and cleanly cut off older OSes from updates as needed.
• Refactored BookWright's squish automation tests for better stability and performance.
• Integrated BookWright with Blurb's API for retrieving photos from various cloud storage services.
• Refactored BookWright's models and views to cleanly support both books and wall art, and to be able to easily implement additional different types of products going forward.
• Optimized many CPU and memory intensive features using profilers to find bottlenecks.
• Documented risks and pain points in various subsystems.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description:
• Continued development of BookWright - Blurb's flagship desktop tool written in C++ and Qt.
• Changed BookWright's project storage from a zip archive to a sqlite database containing a pile of files.
• Integrated a crash reporting library to collect better stack traces and improve BookWright's stability. Fixed may crashes by analyzing these stack traces and implementing improved pointer management.
• Upgraded BookWright's code base to C++11 and dealt with the accompanying dependency and OS support issues.
• Prototyped a functioning apple store version of BookWright. This involved tightening file system access, managing the application package through xcode, and converting to a single process application.
• Planned and implemented many refactors to improve the quality and extensibility of the BookWright code base.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
• Designed and built the original prototype for what is now BookWright - Blurb's flagship desktop bookmaking tool. Written in C++ and Qt. Prototype features included full custom book designs, user authentication, and upload to the website using Blurb's APIs. Presented prototype to Chief Product Officer.
• Onboarded colleagues to the BookWright code base.
• Built the initial release of BookWright with said colleagues.
• Built a cross platform auto-updater for BookWright.
• Built a backend converter to turn pdfs into Blurb's book format. Written in C++ with mupdf. Used heuristics to group text into paragraphs and flatten vector art into images.
• Built the backend process for cropping and formatting our book pdfs into Blurb's "Instant PDF" product.
• Collaborated on a backend converter to turn Blurb's internal book format into ebooks. Written in Java.

projects.title: BookWright
projects.description:
BookWright is built using C++ and Qt. The UI is based on Qt's widget framework.

This is Blurb's flagship desktop book making tool. My involvement in its development has been extensive. I wrote the original prototype back in 2011 (which was of sufficient quality that we built on it). I believe my contributions account for a majority of the code. I have am also heavily involved in the design of the code on major features and systems, even when others carry out the implementation. In addition to programming it, I have contributed substantially to the user-facing design of many of its features.

projects.title: Photo Pruner
projects.description:
Developed with C++ and Qt (QML). All internal business logic is in C++, all UI code is in QML.

A simple application for labelling, sorting, viewing, and deleting photos from a directory. The goal was to be able to more efficiently decide which photos I wanted to keep and which ones I wanted to delete. Sort of like an extremely stripped down version of Adobe Lightroom.

Initial commit was 12/25/2014. Final commit was 1/4/2015.
